live_reference_principles.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — The Printed Image in China
live_reference_principles.applied_principle: woodblock transfer begins from brush-drawn/written forms and carves away blank areas; borrow chisel/relief logic, not texture noise

live_reference_principles.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Yan Family Temple Stele
live_reference_principles.applied_principle: square public-inscription structure with articulated turns, hooks and dots; preserve Chinese-script readability

live_reference_principles.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Model Calligraphies / rubbings
live_reference_principles.applied_principle: stone engraving/rubbing emphasizes controlled positive-negative shape and precise carved structure

live_reference_principles.source: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — On the Seventeenth Day
live_reference_principles.applied_principle: borrow continuity/movement relationships only; do not deconstruct Chinese script

construction: redrew 茶 and 作 from scratch as explicit component/stroke vectors rather than using a typeface outline
used square public-inscription proportions with systematic chisel-cut terminals
used trapezoidal stroke bodies, slightly flared horizontals and blunt falling strokes as intrinsic structure
shared the same terminal grammar across both glyphs instead of attaching a separate decorative line
kept each Chinese component legible and separate enough to inspect/edit

execution.route: manual low-node filled-vector component redraw in Figma
